newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia needs 50 bln kuna to build roads by 2005.
newsitem.headline: Croatia needs 50 bln kuna to build roads by 2005.

text.p: ZAGREB, Feb 3 (Zagreb) - Croatia needs almost 50 billion kuna ($8.5 billion) or 4.6 billion kuna a year to invest into an ambitious road development strategy by year 2005, Aleksandar Caklovic, director of the state road corporation Hrvatske Ceste, said on Monday.
"Such an amount cannot be secured from the budget," he told the daily Vjesnik.
He added it would be necessary to raise part of the money through foreign loans and concessions.

Croatia is negotiating with Slovenia to build a quicker road between its key northern Adriatic port of Rijeka and Trieste in Italy, as well as a Slovene section of the Phyrn motorway from Germany to the Adriatic, Caklovic said.
According to recent media reports, a number of investors from neighbouring Italy and France are interested in concession deals for key routes which might be backed up by foreign banks.
No one at Hrvatske Ceste was available for comment.
French construction firm Buoygues was the first foreign firm to get a concession two years ago to build a so-called Y-road through the tourist Istrian peninsula.
Croatia is now planning to build some 1,400 km of new motorways and 200 km semi-motorways to secure its linking to the main European road routes.
A modern cross-country motorway linking the Adriatic coast with central Europe through Hungary is the first such strategic road, Vjesnik said.
It quoted Caklovic as saying it was a "priority route". The first Rijeka-Zagreb stretch is well under way and should be completed before the start of this summer's tourist season
